NONE: › harmful or limiting
有害的；不利的；限制性的

example: Excessive managerial control is inimical to creative expression.
過度的管制不利於表現創造力。

NONE: › very unusual or of very high quality and therefore impossible to copy
無雙的，無與倫比的；無法模仿的

example: He was describing, in his own inimitable style/way, how to write a best-selling novel.
他以其獨特的風格描述了怎樣寫暢銷小說。
She appeared at the Oscars wearing one of Versace's inimitable creations.
她身著獨一無二的凡賽斯晚裝亮相奧斯卡頒獎典禮。

NONE: › very wrong and unfair
極其錯誤的；極不公正的

example: It is an iniquitous system that allows a person to die because they have no money to pay for medicine.
付不起醫藥費就可置人生死於不顧，這是極其不公的制度。

NONE: › a very wrong and unfair action or situation
極其錯誤；極不公正

example: They fought long and hard against the iniquities of apartheid.
他們為反抗不公正的種族隔離進行了長期艱苦的鬥爭。
The writer reflects on human injustice and iniquity.
這位作家探討了人類的不公正與邪惡。

NONE: B2 of or at the beginning
開始的，最初的
B1 the first letter of a name, especially when used to represent a name
（姓名的）首字母
› to write your initials on something
在…上簽署姓名的首字母

example: My initial surprise was soon replaced by delight.
我最初的驚訝很快變成了興奮。
Initial reports say that seven people have died, though this has not yet been confirmed.
最初的報道說有七人喪生，但這個消息還未得到證實。
He wrote his initials, P.M.R., at the bottom of the page.
他在頁尾寫上了他名字的首字母P.M.R.。
Paul M. Reynolds refused to say what the initial "M" stood for.
保羅‧M‧雷諾茲拒絕說出首字母M代表甚麼意思。
They carved their initials into a tree.
他們把自己名字的首字母刻在樹上。
If you make any changes to the document, please initial them.
如果你修改了文件，請簽上你姓名的首字母。

NONE: › to set the numbers, amounts, etc. in a computer program so that it is ready to start working
預置；使初始化
B2 at the beginning
起初，最初，初時

example: Initially, most people approved of the new plan.
起初，大部分人都同意這個新方案。
The damage was far more serious than initially believed.
損失比開始認為的要嚴重得多。

T: C2 formal to cause something to begin
› to teach someone about an area of knowledge, or to allow someone into a group by a special ceremony
向（某人）傳授專門知識；（透過某種儀式）接納（新會員）

NONE: › a person who has recently joined a group and has been taught its secrets
新入會的人；新成員

example: Who initiated the violence?
誰先使用暴力的？
At the age of eleven, Harry was initiated into the art of golf by his father.
哈裡11歲時，他的父親教他高爾夫球基本技巧。
Each culture had a special ritual to initiate boys into manhood.
每種文化都有特殊的男孩成人禮。

U: › [ U ] formal an occasion when something starts

C or U: › [ C or U ] an occasion when someone is first introduced to an activity or skill
（某項活動或技能的）入門，初學

example: Lawyers for the couple have announced the initiation of divorce proceedings.
夫婦雙方的律師已聲明進入離婚訴訟程序。
My initiation into the mysteries of home brewing was not a success.
我初學自家釀酒並不成功。

NONE: › a process or event that a person takes part in to become an official member of a group
入會儀式

C: C1 [ C ] a new plan or process to achieve something or solve a problem

U: C1 [ U ] the ability to use your judgment to make decisions and do things without needing to be told what to do
主動性；自主決斷行事的能力
› If you do something on your own initiative, you plan it and decide to do it yourself without anyone telling you what to do.

NONE: › the power or opportunity to win an advantage
主動權

example: The peace initiative was welcomed by both sides.
和平倡議受到了雙方的歡迎。

她雖然很年輕，但工作積極主動，一年後就獲提拔為經理。
I shouldn't always have to tell you what to do, use your initiative (= use your own judgment to decide what to do)!
不能總讓我告訴你該做甚麼，你應該有自己的判斷！
to seize/take/lose the initiative
掌握／採取／失去主動權

NONE: › a person who causes something to begin
發起人；創始人
